Profiles, sub-states and tags

What kind of rising is this? The characteristics vector that describes a market day in the trader's terms, the profile that says what each state looks like and where today sits in it, the discovery procedure that finds stable sub-states inside a state without being told what to look for (and doubles as a detector of label error), and the tags the desk declares in advance — correlation sign, event window, pinned, intervention risk — that split a state's ladder wherever the split has the episodes to stand.

1Where a state is, and what it looks like built · validated on synthetic

A named state is a region of a two-dimensional score. That says where the market is on a stress scale and which way it is moving; it says nothing about what kind of rising this is — dollar-led or idiosyncratic, with equities or against them, with vol bid on rallies or on sell-offs. The trader's first question about a label is that one, and it decides which component the label is good or bad for. Three tools answer it, in increasing order of how much they are allowed to change the number on the card:

  1. The state profile describes each state in terms of a daily characteristics vector — always shown, never conditions anything.
  2. Sub-states are clusters discovered inside a state on that vector without being told what to look for — descriptive until, separately, conditioning on them beats the parent out of sample.
  3. Tags are qualifiers the desk declares in advance (correlation sign, event window, pinned, intervention risk) — they split a state's ladder wherever the split has enough episodes.

2The characteristics vector built · validated on synthetic

Daily, trailing, point-in-time, in three groups. Every entry is a plain function of the market frame over a 20-day window (config), so it passes the same truncation test as a feature and can be computed for any day of the history.

3The state profile built · validated on synthetic

For each characteristic and state: the mean inside the state against the mean over all days, in units of the all-days standard deviation — the standardised difference d. Ranked by |d|, the top three are what distinguishes the state; describe turns them into a phrase for the card.

d_(c,s) = ( mean of c on days in state s − mean of c on all days ) / sd of c on all days
  • carry — term_slope low (-1.0σ) · rr_level high (+1.0σ) · fly_level low (-0.9σ)
  • rising — corr_vol_dxy high (+0.3σ) · corr_spot_gold high (+0.3σ) · spotvol_corr low (-0.3σ)
  • agitated — term_slope high (+0.5σ) · spotvol_corr high (+0.3σ) · spotvol_beta high (+0.3σ)
  • stressed — fly_level high (+2.2σ) · rr_level low (-2.1σ) · term_slope high (+1.7σ)
  • normalising — fly_level high (+1.0σ) · volofvol high (+0.9σ) · term_slope high (+0.8σ)
  • settling — vrp low (-0.5σ) · term_slope low (-0.5σ) · fly_level low (-0.5σ)

The card's phrase for each true state, from the top three distinguishing characteristics.

Today's placement

The profile says what the state usually looks like; the card also needs to say whether today is a typical day of it. today_placement gives, for each characteristic, today's value and its percentile within the state's own history — a day at the 99th percentile of spot-equity correlation inside agitated is a different agitated from the median one, and the trader should see that before the number.

4Sub-state discovery built · validated on synthetic

Inside one named state, the days are clustered on the standardised characteristics vector with k-means (k-means++ seeding, six restarts, k = 2…4). A sub-state is allowed to exist only if three conditions hold at once:

  1. Preferred by BIC. A spherical-cluster BIC proxy must prefer k > 1 — a weak condition on its own; it almost always does.
  2. Enough episodes. Every cluster must appear in at least five contiguous runs. A cluster that is one long stretch of one year is a period, not a sub-state.
  3. Stable across episodes. The clustering fitted on a random half of the state's episodes and the clustering fitted on the other half must assign the same cluster to at least 70% of days, averaged over five random splits. Splitting by episode rather than by day matters: days inside one episode are near-duplicates of each other, so a day-level split would flatter any clustering; and a single first-half / second-half split (the first draft) is one noisy draw — on one seed it sat at 0.67 for a split that is real.

Fail any one and k = 1: the named state stands alone. When a sub-state does exist it is named automatically from the two characteristics that most distinguish it from the rest of the state — "rising-2 · corr_spot_eq ↑ · corr_spot_vix ↓" — so that the card's phrase says what the cluster is, not that it is cluster 2.

Sub-states and the number on the card. A sub-state is descriptive — shown in the profile panel with its name and stability — until, separately, the ladder conditioned on it beats the parent state's ladder out of sample (benchmark layer 2b in the validation plan). Only then does it enter the number. The default is that it does not.

5Discovery as a label-impurity detector built · validated on synthetic

Run inside the estimated states, discovery finds something else as well: the days the labeller got wrong. A cluster inside estimated carry whose characteristics look like settling is, in truth, mostly settling. The table runs discovery inside each estimated state and, where it splits, shows which true state each cluster is mostly made of.

This is a diagnostic, not a correction: the labels are not relabelled by their clusters. But on real data, where there is no true state to compare with, a stable cluster inside a state whose profile reads like a neighbour is the clearest evidence available that the labeller is late or the boundary is misplaced, and it points to which one.

6Tags built · validated on synthetic

Two agitated markets with the same score can be opposite trades for a skew position. Six states cannot carry that distinction and more states would starve the cells; discovery may or may not find it. A tag is a qualifier the desk declares in advance, computed point-in-time, that never changes the state but splits a state's ladder into state·tag cells wherever the split has enough evidence.

tagvaluesruleconfig
corr_signneg · flat · pos21-day correlation of spot returns with ΔATM, cut at ±band with hysteresis δ; starts flatwindow 21, band 0.2, δ 0.05
event_windowpre · post · nonethe N business days up to and including a scheduled event, and M after; events from a calendar the desk supplies — known in advance, so point-in-time by constructionbefore 3, after 1, events per pair
pinnedpinned · nonerealised / implied < r and the 21-day high-low range < q × the range implied vol would suggest (2σ√(21/252)) — the market paying for movement it is not getting; long-gamma P&L dies here firstrv_ratio 0.6, range_ratio 0.6
intervention_riskrisk · nonepair-specific: spot has moved more than m in the leaning-against direction over w days, or sits beyond a level, or an official-comment / rate-check flag from the adapter is setper pair: direction, move 5% / 21d, level, flag column

The split rule

The regime series becomes state·tag where the tag is non-neutral, and stays the plain state where it is neutral (flat, none). Each tagged cell is then counted: a cell with fewer than five episodes collapses back to its parent state. So a tag adds cells only for the condition it names and only where the condition recurs; it can never multiply the cells until nothing is estimable.

10On real data built · validated on synthetic WU-06b, WU-08d, WU-11

  1. Build the characteristics on the real frame first (WU-06b) and look at the profile heatmap from the estimated labels before anything else: if stressed does not read as steep skew and inverted term structure, the labels are not describing the market the desk sees, whatever Gate 2 says.
  2. Expect discovery to find little, and treat what it finds as a question. On real data the candidates inside rising are the ones traders already name — dollar-led risk-off, rates-led, an idiosyncratic pair event, a carry unwind, commodity- or EM-led — and discovery should be made to show which of them are stable. Run it inside the estimated states as well, as the impurity detector of Section 5.
  3. Declare tags before looking at ladders. The thresholds in configs/default.yaml › tags and the per-pair intervention configs (D17) are set from desk knowledge, not tuned to outcomes; the cell table says which cells have the episodes to stand.
  4. A sub-state or a tag enters the number only through layer 2b — conditioning on it beats the parent out of sample at h ≤ 10 — and only with the continuous score in the baseline, for the same reason that applies to leading features: otherwise it is rewarded for finding the labeller's errors.
  5. Failure modes. A cross-asset series with a different cut time (correlations biased toward zero — fix the adapter); stability that is high for one k and one seed only (raise n_splits); a tag whose cells all collapse (the condition is rarer than thought, or the window is wrong); a tag that never reads neutral (the dead band is too narrow).
